National framework applies in full: no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections exist for sexual orientation or gender identity, legal gender change requires sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval, and the 2022 penal-code amendment criminalising sex outside marriage — in force from 2 January 2026 — carries up to one year's imprisonment, so same-sex couples have no recognised legal relationship. National reporting (August 2026) describes vigilante mobs attacking transgender people while the government takes steps to codify anti-LGBT provisions, and the record is scored relative to the national score of 0.15.

A documented provincial enforcement signal is the only sub-national divergence: in February 2025 a transgender content creator became the first transgender detainee held in this province's women's prison after her file was declared complete on suspected defamation/extortion — an authority placing a trans woman in a facility by identity rather than legal sex, contrary to the usual national pattern. Otherwise the province is a conservative religious-education heartland with no other sub-national signal documented.
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Parent-nation policy turbulence: the government is taking steps to codify anti-LGBT provisions, the amended penal code comes into force on 2 January 2026, and the parent nation voted in 2016, 2022 and 2025 against the independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity.

rewrites.summary:
National framework applies in full in the capital: same-sex "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" is criminalised under the 1936 penal code with up to 20 years' imprisonment plus whipping, the "gross indecency" offence carries up to two years, and enforcement with arrests, prosecutions and corporal punishment is documented since the 2018 election.

Local enforcement in the capital is documented on the ground: on 28 November the capital police, the city administration and the national religious department arrested over 200 people at an all-male health centre in the capital — a visible, high-volume enforcement signal a visitor could encounter. The national score of 0.16 is used, with the capital's concentrated scene and greater anonymity read as the model delta (route 3).
rewrites.tangentialFactors:
Litigation flux in the parent nation: the national apex court has struck down some state religious criminal-code provisions as beyond state power, and the 2022 human-rights report describes regression as a conservative strand of religion gains ground in the parent nation.

Neighbour comparison: every state and the federal territories of the capital and a neighbouring administrative centre apply Sharia (religious) codes that typically criminalise same-sex conduct, so no safer enclave for this province is documented in the sources.
rewrites.localsOnly: Resident-facing evidence: the 2022 human-rights report is based on interviews with 73 LGBT people between 2018 and 2021, including people living in the capital, and it documents discrimination against residents backed by arrests and prosecutions. It quotes a local activist describing regression as a conservative strand of religion gains ground. These are resident-facing enforcement and attitude findings rather than visitor-specific data.
